newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea's Feb note default ratio hits 15-year high.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea's Feb note default ratio hits 15-year high.

text.p: South Korea's promissory note default ratio rose to 0.24 pct in February from 0.21 percent in January, the central Bank of Korea said on Friday.
It is the highest ratio in 15 years.
The bank said in a statement the ratio rose after Hanbo Steel Co and its affiliates began to fail to honour such notes since late January.
Hanbo Steel, the flagship of the nation's 14 largest conglomerate, defaulted on repayments of promissory notes on January 23 under a $5.8 billion loan.
But the number of defaulting companies fell to 1,060 in February, compared with 1,115 in January, the central bank said.
